evals.prompt: We launch the order service next month and then want to spend a quarter paying down tech debt. Can you do a technical debt audit of evals/files/sample-repo and tell us what to clean up first? It's an export without a .git folder, so use evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json as the git history (the scripts take it with --history). The test-coverage and dependency audits already ran and their findings are in sample-repo/audit/findings.
evals.expected_output: Runs complexity.py, churn.py --history evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json (10-commit window), todo_age.py --history, duplicates.py, dead_code.py, eol_check.py, suppressions.py, docs_check.py --history, ../audit-code-scan/scripts/grep_scan.py with scripts/patterns/dotnet.json, and debt_score.py. Report contains: a debt inventory table (item, category, location, age, impact, effort, priority, bucket) ranked with OrderImportService.ImportOrders first (hotspot: ~405 lines, CC ~118, changed in 8 of the last 10 commits); the near-identical CalculateInvoiceTotal / CalculateQuoteTotal pair; the unused LegacyCsvExporter module; the Program.cs:15 TODO aged over 3 years (2023-06-14); IdentityServer4 4.1.2 past end-of-life (2022-12-13); plus smaller items (WebClient deprecated API with its SYSLIB0014 pragma, commented-out block in QuoteService, mixed Newtonsoft/System.Text.Json, stale README with dangling paths, no runbook/ADRs). A hotspot table with ImportOrders at rank 1. A roadmap split into quick wins / next quarter / long term. A maintainability score with each input, its weight and contribution (quality-findings input excluded because those skills did not run). Consumed TEST-001 and DEP-001 appear as inventory rows referencing their ids and are not re-flagged; audit-frontend-best-practices, audit-orm-query-and-data-access, audit-async-and-dependency-injection, audit-backend-resource-leak, audit-frontend-memory-leak and audit-system-design are listed as not run. findings.json holds only launch risks: DEBT High for IdentityServer4 EOL and DEBT Medium for the untested hotspot.
expectations: The skill passes evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json to the history-aware scripts (--history) instead of failing for lack of .git
The debt inventory ranks OrderImportService.ImportOrders first and describes it as both complex (hundreds of lines, very high cyclomatic complexity) and changed in 8 of the last 10 commits
The churn-vs-complexity hotspot list shows ImportOrders at rank 1
CalculateInvoiceTotal (PricingService) and CalculateQuoteTotal (QuoteService) are reported as near-identical / duplicated functions
LegacyCsvExporter is reported as an unused / unreferenced module, with a note that dead-code detection is heuristic
The TODO at OrderService.Api/Program.cs:15 is reported with an age of more than three years from blame
IdentityServer4 4.1.2 is reported as past end-of-life, and the EOL table's as-of date is mentioned
The roadmap has three sections: quick wins, next quarter, long term
A single maintainability score is given with its inputs and weights explained
TEST-001 and DEP-001 are mapped into the inventory by id and not duplicated as new DEBT findings; Newtonsoft.Json is not reported as end-of-life
OrdersController, Config and the Models classes are not reported as dead code
findings.json contains only launch-risk DEBT findings (IdentityServer4 EOL, untested hotspot) and validates with ../audit-finding-writer/scripts/findings.py validate

evals.prompt: Where should we refactor first in evals/files/sample-repo? I want the files or functions that are both complicated and constantly changing. No .git in that folder - history is in evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json, pass it with --history and use the last 10 commits.
evals.expected_output: Runs complexity.py then churn.py --history evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json --last-commits 10. Hotspot list: #1 ImportOrders in OrderImportService.cs (8 commits x CC ~118, score far above the rest), then OrdersController.cs (3 commits, low complexity), QuoteService.cs and PricingService.cs (1 commit each). Explains the score (commits x cyclomatic complexity) and why low-complexity files with some churn and complex code without churn rank lower. Recommends a first slice for ImportOrders (characterization tests, then extracting validation, pricing, tax, FX and stock allocation) and notes there are no tests (TEST-001). Mentions that function-level churn comes from the synthetic history's function names.
expectations: Uses --history evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json with a 10-commit window
Ranks ImportOrders (OrderImportService.cs) first with 8 commits in the window
States the hotspot score formula (change frequency multiplied by complexity)
Proposes an incremental first step such as characterization tests before extracting parts of ImportOrders
Does not rank LegacyCsvExporter as a hotspot (no commits in the window)

evals.prompt: Quick one on evals/files/sample-repo: are we on any end-of-life runtimes, frameworks or packages, and how old are the TODOs in the code? The folder has no git metadata; use evals/files/synthetic-git-history.json via --history for blame dates.

expectations: Reports IdentityServer4 4.1.2 as past end-of-life with its EOL date
Does not report net10.0, Newtonsoft.Json or Swashbuckle.AspNetCore as end-of-life
States the as-of date of the bundled EOL table and that it needs periodic refresh
Reports the Program.cs TODO as more than three years old and the OrderImportService.cs TODO as recent, using blame data from the synthetic history
Lists TODOs with location, age and text
